title: Falcon 9 USSF-266 (SLC-4E)

azimuth_deg.derived: Great-circle bearing from the LL2 SLC-4E pad to the vertex-average centroid of NOTAM NTTT A1483/26 (space debris return of SpaceX USSF266-TH3). Vertices 30-00S 135-51W, 27-48S 136-13W, 27-19S 133-10W, 30-00S 132-35W. Centroid 28.779S 134.454W. Bearing 193.41 deg, 7199 km. Non-rotating inclination 101.00 deg. The 24 Nov period on that notice is 1740-2218Z, which starts 1 h 45 min after the 15:55Z window open. No nearer ascent polygon (a ZLA Area A) was found.

payload_kg.note: FITTED inside the Falcon 9 config bounds (13.0-21.6 t, themselves a Starlink V2 mini band) so the BORROWED SECO-1 time can reach the BORROWED parking altitude. USSF-266 mass is unpublished. The fitted number is an ASSUMPTION of the fit, not an estimate of the payload. No satellite count is used.

insertion_alt_km.assumption: USSF-266 orbit is unpublished. 177.3 km perigee is borrowed from the Starlink Group 15-18 parking orbit used for USSF-317, because this flight's published times through fairing match the sl-15-16 family timeline that produced that orbit (MECO 2:26, SES-1 2:36, fairing 2:56, SECO-1 8:39). It is not a USSF-266 element. Inclination is not tuned; the 193.41 deg debris azimuth stands.

apoapsis_alt_km.assumption: Same borrowed Group 15-18 parking apogee. Not a USSF-266 source.

target.altitude_reference: equatorial-radius (r - 6378.137 km) for SMA; insertion altitude residual uses geodetic altitude

header_notes: ILLUSTRATIVE. PRE-FLIGHT. USSF-266, Falcon 9, SLC-4E. T0 is the window open 2026-11-24T15:55:00Z (Tue 24 Nov 7:55 a.m. PT). SpaceX https://www.spacex.com/launches/ussf266: four-hour window to 19:55Z. Backup Wed 25 Nov 7:46 a.m. PT = 2026-11-25T15:46:00Z. 29th flight of the first stage. Landing on Of Course I Still Love You. LL2 id 460d9db7-eaf6-4cd9-b095-cff433534c09 status Go at 15:55Z.

Published timeline (SpaceX ussf266): Max-Q 1:07, MECO 2:26, stage sep 2:29, SES-1 2:36, fairing 2:56, entry burn 6:03-6:27, landing burn 8:01, landing 8:23. SECO, orbit and deploy are not published. Payload is classified. No unofficial satellite count is used.

AZIMUTH CONFLICT recorded, not averaged. NOTAM MMFO B4504/26 is the stage-1 reentry box (centroid bearing about 169.4 deg, 672 km). A constant-azimuth rhumb at 193.41 deg does not pass through that box (about 280 km cross-track at 670 km). The stage-1 box was not used for the azimuth, the same rule as NROL-136. Its 24 Nov period is 1555-2038Z, the older FAA backup close, not the current 1955Z window close.

INFERRED/ASSUMED: SECO-1 at T+519 s and a 177 x 266 km parking orbit are borrowed from the sl-15-16 / Group 15 family, not from USSF-266. File ends 2 revs after cutoff (deploy unpublished). Booster entry and landing are not modelled.

final_cutoff_s.assumption: USSF-266 SECO-1 is unpublished. T+8:39 is borrowed from https://www.spacex.com/launches/sl-15-16 because MECO, SES-1 and fairing on the USSF-266 page match that timeline. Stage separation here is 2:29, one second earlier than sl-15-16's 2:30.

knots.src: https://github.com/shahar603/Telemetry-Data/tree/master/Iridium%20NEXT%207 (SpaceX webcast telemetry; FAMILY stand-in, not this flight). This flight's published MECO is also T+146 s.
same. This flight's published SES-1 is also T+156 s.
same. This flight's published fairing separation is also T+176 s.

cd.assumption: same Cd as the ascent fit (fixed 0.4)

deploy.note: SpaceX publishes no SECO, restart or deploy time for USSF-266 (classified payload). Propagated 2 revs on the inferred insertion orbit. The insertion altitude is borrowed, not a USSF-266 element.

fitted.method: scipy least_squares (TRF, bounded) vs published knots + target orbit

payload_kg.basis: 27 V2 Mini Optimized: ~575 kg each community-reported (spacex.com.pl) = 15.5 t; MaxQ lists 800 kg each = 21.6 t (upper bound). Mass not published by SpaceX
